title: Recurring unresolved limitation 'self-report-bias' across 6 independent papers

Screen time measures relied on self-reported survey responses, which may be influenced by extreme mischievous responding.
Self-reported data regarding time spent on social media and sleep measures may lack accuracy or be subject to reporting bias.

All measures were based on self-reports, which may deviate from actual time spent on social media.
Reliance on self-report survey measures across all reviewed studies introduces potential memory inaccuracies, social desirability bias, and cultural response style bias.

consumer.headline: 6 separate teams ran into the same wall: self report bias
consumer.kind_short: A problem that several independent teams ran into
consumer.kind_long: Papers describe the limits of their own work. When separate teams — who did not build on each other — keep reporting the same limit, that is a sign of a real obstacle rather than one group's bad luck.
consumer.strength_meaning: Several independent papers point at this, and we could read their full text to check.
consumer.why: 6 separate research teams each reported hitting this in their own work. They did not build on each other, so this is unlikely to be one group's bad luck. Their papers span 1 years. We could read 6 of them in full, which is where teams describe what actually went wrong.
